scope: Local and shared-development producer proof. This file grants no external or production authority.

control.file: Regular, non-symlink, current OS user owned, no group or other permissions, outside checkout.
control.identity: Current uid and hostname, unexpired exact operation list and development context.
control.database: Pinned shared-development direct endpoint plus matching current database, role and explicit schema. Neither a URL nor a sentinel alone grants authority.
control.migration_role: Operator only. The application runtime cannot create schema objects or update migration history.

migration_provenance.deployment_path: Vercel project everyfield has root apps/web and default Next build. app build/start and managed previews do not run migrations. CI migrates its throwaway database explicitly.
migration_provenance.automatic_replay: Only a complete matching ordered checksum prefix is replayed. Unknown, missing or changed checksums refuse before application.
migration_provenance.adoption: Separately review the exact existing rows and SQL hashes. The explicit command preserves applied_at and marks adopted, never original. It never runs at startup or migration replay.
migration_provenance.production: No production history was read or changed. A future explicit production migration needs owner-approved adoption first. This development-only CLI refuses production.

http.liveness: /api/health returns process status and UTC time only, private no-store.
http.executor: /api/cron/jobs runs every minute from apps/web/vercel.json with the CRON_SECRET bearer. It closes lost Evry jobs and runs one bounded batch of every job kind that has a worker; the schedule grants no domain authority. Before any mail is sent, `mail-expiry` cancels stale queued mail that was never handed off: password-reset and sign-up verification links older than the one hour they work, and task or meeting reminders a day past their slot. Every mount that queues mail then has a sending pass through the real queued transport (Resend with a key, else the capture outbox), each claiming only its own logical-key prefixes (MAIL_PASSES in apps/web/src/server/jobs/mail.ts) and rechecking each mail under its mount's rule just before the handoff: church invitations (`mail`), identity (`identity-mail`), organization connections (`organization-mail`), settings (`settings-mail`), onboarding and association receipts (`onboarding-mail`), task, phase, meeting and milestone notices (`notice-mail`) and digests (`digest-mail`). Each pass first replays its mail whose handoff answered unknown on an earlier tick, with the same stored request and idempotency key, only inside the provider's 23 h 55 min window; past it the mail stays in reconcile, unclaimed, for a provider callback. Scheduled Messages email is handed to the provider at its send time (`messages`); Messages "Check result" re-sends a batch that answered unknown under its original key inside the same window. Last, `mail-callbacks` applies stored provider callbacks whose email now has its provider id. Each step's outcome is in the tick's `steps` body.
http.callback: /api/webhooks/resend is the one mail callback endpoint. It reads at most 16,384 bytes, verifies the Resend (svix) signature once and stores a durable safe receipt before applying it. A correctly signed event of a type it does not handle (for example email.delivery_delayed) answers 200 and changes nothing; a badly signed request is refused. It is not mounted without RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET: it answers 404 unavailable. No live subscription or credentials are configured here.
http.execution: One same-app Next Node invocation per minute from Vercel cron, at most 300 seconds, WP-031 batch bounds. No standalone worker.
http.activation: Integrating feature owners supply actual handlers and current authorization. Explicit owner approval is required before live subscription, Vercel schedule or provider settings.

observability.operator: Trusted host/session adapters supply freshly verified exact immutable principal, tenant, purpose and allowed operations. Tenant roles and recovery_operator do not imply broad investigation access. Inspection appends safe attribution in the same transaction.
observability.telemetry: Optional explicit endpoint, HTTPS except loopback, no credentials/query/fragment in URL, no implicit provider. Closed content-free fields and bounded flush; no raw errors, prompts, mail, files or private-care existence.
observability.readiness: Actual selected probes distinguish ready, unavailable, behind, unconfigured and unverified. Missing provider or backup proof stays visible. No customer SLA follows from liveness.

recovery.live_gate: G-RECOVERY remains open. recovery.mts holds only the offline candidate manifest check (shape, expiry and duplicate identities); no test, encryption or byte check here proves recovery.
recovery.future_restricted_host: Before customer data, positively identify the approved restricted host and schedule, deliver dedicated bucket-scoped credentials and recoverable keys outside ordinary app/build/preview, and prove negative access.
recovery.future_provider_proof: Verify Neon seven-day PITR and expiring daily snapshots, Tigris seven-day deleted-object retention and cleanup, separate private encrypted daily backup bucket, exact DB and ready-byte inventory, current witness journal synchronized at least every five minutes, original subject expiry and external receipt reconciliation.
recovery.restore: No restore runs here. Keep users/jobs/mail/issues disabled in an isolated drill. Apply authoritative current pending/cancelled/purged witnesses, verify matching bytes and original expiry, reconcile provider facts, and only then seek explicit reopening authority.
recovery.measurements: Ordinary live-provider targets are at most one-hour lost work and four-hour recovery. A surviving fresh complete accessible daily copy may permit at most 24-hour fallback. None is measured or guaranteed by this change. Shared-provider/account failure risk remains; no disaster RTO or customer SLA.
recovery.spending: No added paid plan, service or account. G-SPEND remains open; obtain explicit approval of a concrete low/expected/high monthly cost and usage envelope before commitment.

downstream: WP-005 and UI owners connect the tested internal fixture-session adapter through a development-only transport with the exact managed target and fresh synthetic allowlist. No switching surface exists in production.
Lifecycle/document owners supply complete registered purge/restore consumers and inverse fixtures before lifecycle closure.
WP-042 runs actual pinned synthetic fleet evaluations; proof inspection never runs a model or authorizes rollout.
WP-049 supplies safe feedback publication and the actual owner workflow handoff; no engineering board integration is enabled.
WP-058 closes cross-domain integration and authorized customer-data gates with actual evidence.
